confidence_note: Passages checked in George Long's translation: 11.33 (fig in winter), 11.34 (Epictetus: whisper 'To-morrow perchance thou wilt die' when kissing a child; bad omen objection; ears of corn), 11.35 (grapes), 7.27 (think of what you have, but don't overvalue), 2.11 (may depart this moment; gods). The Latin label 'premeditatio malorum' does not appear in Meditations (written in Greek) and is only mentioned as a later name, not attributed to Marcus. The old text's invented quote ('say this was a trust left to me') and the claim that he daily imagined losing health and empire were dropped.
facts: 11.34: Epictetus said a man kissing his child should whisper 'To-morrow perchance thou wilt die'; objection: words of bad omen; reply: no word expressing a work of nature is ill-omened, or it would be ill-omened to speak of ears of corn being reaped.
11.33: to look for a fig in winter is a madman's act; so is looking for one's child when it is no longer allowed.
11.35: the unripe grape, the ripe bunch, the dried grape: all changes into something which exists not yet.
7.27: think less of what you lack than of what you have; pick the best and reflect how eagerly you'd seek them if absent; but don't overvalue them so as to be disturbed if you lose them.
2.11: since you may depart life this very moment, regulate every act and thought accordingly; if there are gods, leaving is not to be feared.
Meditations was written in Greek; the Latin term for this practice does not appear in it.
scene_details: unripe grape, ripe bunch, dried grape
tension: A loving gesture paired with a thought of death, defended as natural.
opening_idea: Open on 7.27, the corn reply, the grapes, or the whisper.

lessons.idea: Briefly picture something you have as gone; you see its value and cling less.

reflect_final: Which person you see daily could you greet differently if you imagined missing them?

use_cases.move: Recall Marcus's whisper and pause for a hug.
Ask how much you'd miss it before shopping.
Share Marcus's reminder and suggest a call.

pocket_idea: Look at something you love and think how eagerly you'd search for it if it were gone.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Marcus Aurelius copied Epictetus's advice to whisper 'tomorrow you may die' while kissing your child.
